intro.title: Generic useFetch<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useFetch<T>` that fetches data from an API and returns it in a type-safe way. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics to create a flexible hook that can handle different data structures, like users or posts, while keeping your code strongly typed. The main technologies involved are React hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`) and TypeScript's generic syntax (`<T>`). By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that manages loading, error, and data states for any API endpoint.
intro.usecase: Generic useFetch<T> patterns are essential in modern React applications that display dynamic data from APIs. You'll see this in e-commerce product listings where each item has consistent structure but different data types, dashboard widgets showing various metrics (sales, users, analytics), and admin panels displaying tables of users, orders, or content. This approach allows developers to create reusable data-fetching hooks that maintain type safety across different API endpoints while reducing code duplication.
